answer: A lotus-citation bond: each identity locks 70 credits and files a lotus-sealed citation of earlier work on the ledger. Citations form a spiral: each newcomer cites work at least an epoch old, and the auditor replays the spiral, rejecting reused citations. Forged citations burn the bond. A rented-citation ring fails: 1,000 fakes pay 25,000 in nectar fees plus 70,000 locked against a 40,000 pool; one honest agent pays 25 once, recovers its bond.
